title: ALMA, ATCA, and Spitzer Observations of the Luminous Extragalactic Supernova SN 1978K
question: What is the radio-millimeter spectrum of SN 1978K, and what do ALMA, ATCA and Spitzer data imply for the synchrotron emission and for warm and cold dust?

what.value: AKARI infrared points and dust models of SN 1978K

evidence.quote: The *AKARI* infrared points show SN 1978K on 2006 December 03–04.
shows a source at the location of SN 1978K with a peak brightness of 94 mJy/beam at 200 MHz

recipe.goal: Image ALMA continuum and measure flux densities
recipe.method: Pipeline calibration, mtmfs tclean per SPW, pairs and whole band; point-like source flux
Miriad calibration, robust 0.5 imaging, Gaussian point-source fit; 16 cm band split into four 512 MHz sub-bands

recipe.goal: Spitzer IRAC photometry and light curves
recipe.method: Point source photometry on CBCD with APEX in MOPEX using PRF map; handbook correction factors
Compare modified Montes+1997 parameterized model with a broken power law GRB fireball cooling-break model with wind scaling
key_parameters: Radio decay t^-1.53 gives p=2.373; indices -0.687 below and -1.187 above the break
assumptions: Generic fireball formalism with wind scaling; ISM scaling rejected

recipe.method: Extrapolate synchrotron models back to AKARI epoch, compare with Tanaka+2012 dust models, fit IRAC decay
assumptions: ALMA/ATCA points extrapolated back assuming fireball evolution

answer_key.quantity: ALMA Band 3 flux density (all 4 SPW, 103.5 GHz)

evidence.quote: the non-thermal radio continuum continues to decay as $t^{-1.53}$

answer_key.quantity: Change in spectral index at break

evidence.quote: the change in the spectral index appears to be $\sim 0.5$
The $t^{-2.45}$ power law decay in both channels is much faster than we have found in the radio
